scenarios.title: Interactive Mode (REPL) Basics
scenarios.description: Watch how Python evaluates mathematical operations and basic strings one step at a time.

steps.explanation: The interpreter reads `10 + 20`, evaluates it to 30, and prints it.
Here, we use the `print()` function to output text to the screen.
It reads `5 * 10`, evaluates it to 50, and prints the result.

scenarios.title: Variables & Data Types
scenarios.description: See how variables are stored in memory and how their data types change.

steps.explanation: Python assigns the integer value 20 to the variable 'age'. It automatically knows this is an `int`.
Python assigns a decimal value to 'price'. This makes it a `float`.
'is_student' is assigned a boolean value `True`. Note the capital 'T'!
'name' is assigned a string value. Quotes indicate text data.

scenarios.title: Numbers vs Strings
scenarios.description: A very important difference between mathematical addition and string concatenation.

steps.explanation: Since 20 and 10 are integers, Python performs mathematical addition.
Since "20" and "10" are in quotes, Python treats them as text and joins them together (concatenation).
